observed: Robot walked straight forward into contact with a purple box that was visible only in the leftmost (peripheral) depth column at ~0.7m, while central columns stayed >1m clear.

cause.what: side_memory_seconds is set to 0.0, disabling the hazard map's SIDE kind (hazards.py HazardMap._enabled requires side_memory_seconds > 0). Near-body wall returns in the peripheral sensor column are therefore never remembered or merged into the view ahead, so Forward never starts an avoidance episode for an object alongside the body.

evidence.shows: Purple box already close on the robot's side, 1s before contact, gap 26px, yet approaching.
Box at the robot's left side 0.5s before contact, gap 2px on screen.
Box remains very close at the side through first contact (gap 2px, feet -13.3px past base edge at K4).
Sensor did see the object in its leftmost column: column 0 reads 77cm in the wall rows while column 1 reads ~129cm  the object is peripheral, not in the central front columns.
Object still only in column 0: rows 3-4 read 73/72cm there against 119/120cm in column 1.
Brain stayed in forward at vx=0.24 the whole approach, vyaw only small heading corrections, never brake/turn  it never treated the side object as an obstacle.

Configured side_memory_seconds=0.0 overrides the built-in default of 3.0s, switching off the only mechanism (hazards.py SIDE detection, SIDE_LOOKAHEAD 0.8m / SIDE_BAND 0.30m) that keeps near-body wall returns like this ~0.72m, column-0 return in play.

ruled_out.because: Central front columns read over a metre at t=9.923s and t=10.925s while only column 0 was near; the view ahead was genuinely clear, so the stop-and-turn path correctly never fired.
ruled_out.cause: Head-on wall detection failure / blind sensor

ruled_out.because: Log shows safe=yes on every tick and the state never left forward for hold; valid depth arrived throughout.
ruled_out.cause: Fall, unsafe state, or missing depth frames

ruled_out.because: The object returns 72-77cm readings in the middle/upper rows (rows 3-4) of column 0, i.e. a tall body-height object, not a floor-level return in the bottom rows.
Depth frames are full of valid returns (nearest per row continuous in the log), so the frame was not blind; the near return was present but in the peripheral column only.

fix_direction: Restore a positive side-memory duration in the configuration (the built-in default is 3 seconds) so near-body side returns are retained and fed into avoidance.
explanation: The purple box approached along the robot's flank rather than head-on, so it showed up only at the edge of the robot's depth view while the way straight ahead stayed clear. The robot therefore kept walking its straight line and clipped the box with its side. The safeguard meant to remember things seen close alongside the body was turned off in the settings, so those edge sightings were thrown away instead of making the robot steer away or stop.

plain.camera: The purple box stayed close beside the robot's foot.
plain.robot: The robot kept walking straight forward until contact.
plain.why: Its memory for objects beside its body was off.
